title: How much do the two fish weigh together?
description: A big fish weighs half a kilogram and a small fish weighs a fourth of a kilogram. The half is cut into two fourths so both weights are in the same unit, and the fourths are counted.
teaching_notes: One idea: to add two fractions, write both with the same fractional unit and count the units. Watch for students who add the bottom numbers and write two over six.

source: The big fish weighs 1/2 kg. The small one weighs 1/4 kg. Together they weigh ____ kg.
video_script.why: The child sees one half as two fourths on the same bar, so the two fish weights can be counted in one unit.
video_script.substitution: Cut the half of a kilogram into two equal fourths, so that both fish are measured in fourths of a kilogram.
video_script.anchor: A big fish of one half kilogram and a small fish of one fourth kilogram
video_script.payoff_line: Together the two fish weigh three fourths of a kilogram
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one fourth, three fourths
maths_rules: 1 kg bar cut into 4 equal parts: each part is 1/4 kg
1/2 kg is 2 of those parts, so 1/2 = 1/4 + 1/4
big fish 1/2 kg = 2 parts, small fish 1/4 kg = 1 part, together 3 parts of 1/4 kg
3 x 1/4 = 3/4, so together they weigh 3/4 kg
check: 3/4 kg is less than 1 kg, as 3 parts leave 1 part of the bar empty
video_script.design: One idea: change one half into two fourths and count fourths. Assumes halves and fourths on a bar. The bar of one kilogram stays on the board to the end.
